_comment: 🧩️ BCF 2.1/✳️any's own contribution to the repository test platform — its mutation oracle registration and its declared mutation vocabulary (wave 7, ticket 26/08/23/END-TO-END-TESTING-REFACTOR). A BCF file IS a ZIP of XML markup/viewpoint/snapshot files, and no standalone BCF crate exists in the Rust ecosystem (BCF support only appears bundled inside much larger MPL-licensed IFC toolkits), so the reference here composes the already-linked, genuinely independent `zip` and `quick-xml` crates over the real BCF-XML 2.1 shapes rather than adopting a weaker/unlicensed substitute. Discovered by convention alongside ✏️s/🔌️plugins/🗄️stdio's own top-level manifest; merged into one registry, no central edit required.

oracles.rationale: bcfzip is a flat ZIP of per-topic markup.bcf/.bcfv/snapshot.png parts (no OPC apparatus). `zip` 6 is the reference archive reader/writer, `quick-xml` 0.42 the reference XML reader/writer for every part inside it; composed here into one independent BCF-XML 2.1 reader/writer covering the full 14-kind `BcfMutation` vocabulary this subset declares. Distinct id/capability from the top-level `zip`/`xml` entries' own capabilities: this composition is surveyed specifically for BCF's markup.xsd/visinfo.xsd shapes, not for either library's generic archive/XML capability.

comparisonProfiles.description: BCF 2.1 documents compared by version, every topic keyed by guid (title/description/status/priority/labels/creationDate/creationAuthor, comments keyed by guid, viewpoints keyed by guid), and every raw retained part keyed by name by size+content digest. A viewpoint's camera/components project as their full typed structure; its PNG snapshot projects as size+digest rather than raw bytes (an opaque binary payload, not a lossy-encoded sample array, so a content digest is the correct treatment per the fleet brief's raster precedent). Topic/comment/viewpoint/part identity keys make document-order irrelevant; label/selection/exception/coloring lists are unordered sets in the BCF domain, so all arrays compare as sets.
